title: Distributions — spread, not averages
description: An average hides the nights worth explaining. Everything here is a distribution. The context panels join the `context` table, which is empty until Stage 4 fills it — the queries are already correct and light up on their own.

panels.title: Readiness by weekday — five-number summary
panels.description: Grafana core has no box-plot panel, so this is the same five numbers as a table: min, lower quartile, median, upper quartile, max. Read `n` first — a weekday with two samples has no distribution worth reading.

targets.rawSql:
select
    to_char(day, 'Dy')                                                    as "Weekday",
    count(*)                                                              as "n",
    min(readiness_score)                                                  as "Min",
    round(percentile_cont(0.25) within group (order by readiness_score)::numeric, 1) as "Q1",
    round(percentile_cont(0.50) within group (order by readiness_score)::numeric, 1) as "Median",
    round(percentile_cont(0.75) within group (order by readiness_score)::numeric, 1) as "Q3",
    max(readiness_score)                                                  as "Max",
    round(stddev_samp(readiness_score), 1)                                as "SD"
from daily
where readiness_score is not null
  and $__timeFilter(day)
group by to_char(day, 'Dy'), extract(isodow from day)
order by extract(isodow from day)

panels.title: Readiness by weekday — quartiles
panels.description: The same numbers drawn. The gap between Q1 and Q3 is the point: a weekday with a high median and a wide spread is not a good weekday, it is an inconsistent one.

targets.rawSql:
select
    to_char(day, 'Dy') as "Weekday",
    round(percentile_cont(0.25) within group (order by readiness_score)::numeric, 1) as "Q1",
    round(percentile_cont(0.50) within group (order by readiness_score)::numeric, 1) as "Median",
    round(percentile_cont(0.75) within group (order by readiness_score)::numeric, 1) as "Q3"
from daily
where readiness_score is not null
  and $__timeFilter(day)
group by to_char(day, 'Dy'), extract(isodow from day)
order by extract(isodow from day)

panels.title: Readiness after an evening that ran past 19:00
panels.description: The reason this project exists: Oura cannot see your calendar. Asks when the day *finished*, not when a meeting started — an 18:00–20:30 call does not start after 19:00 but certainly ends after it. Populated by the calendar importer.

targets.rawSql:
-- context_daily resolves the local end hour; "after 19:00" is a wall-clock question
-- and the rows are stored in UTC.
with labelled as (
    select
        d.readiness_score,
        d.hrv_avg,
        d.rhr_lowest,
        case when c.last_end_hour >= 19 then 'Ran past 19:00' else 'Evening free' end as bucket
    from daily d
    left join context_daily c
           on c.day = d.day
          and c.kind = 'meeting'
    where d.readiness_score is not null
      and $__timeFilter(d.day)
)
select
    bucket as "Evening",
    count(*) as "n",
    round(percentile_cont(0.25) within group (order by readiness_score)::numeric, 1) as "Readiness Q1",
    round(percentile_cont(0.50) within group (order by readiness_score)::numeric, 1) as "Readiness median",
    round(percentile_cont(0.75) within group (order by readiness_score)::numeric, 1) as "Readiness Q3",
    round(avg(hrv_avg), 1) as "Mean HRV",
    round(avg(rhr_lowest), 1) as "Mean resting HR"
from labelled
group by bucket
order by bucket

panels.title: Readiness by context kind
panels.description: Generic over whatever lands in `context` — meetings from the calendar, and alcohol, caffeine or naps from Oura's own tags. Compares days a thing happened against days it did not, so a kind only appears once it has data.

targets.rawSql:
with days as (
    select day, readiness_score, sleep_score, hrv_avg
    from daily
    where readiness_score is not null and $__timeFilter(day)
),
tagged as (
    select distinct kind, day from context_daily
)
select
    t.kind as "Context",
    count(*) as "Days with",
    round(avg(d.readiness_score), 1) as "Readiness (with)",
    (select round(avg(readiness_score), 1) from days x
      where not exists (select 1 from tagged y where y.kind = t.kind and y.day = x.day)) as "Readiness (without)",
    round(avg(d.hrv_avg), 1) as "HRV (with)",
    (select round(avg(hrv_avg), 1) from days x
      where not exists (select 1 from tagged y where y.kind = t.kind and y.day = x.day)) as "HRV (without)"
from tagged t
join days d on d.day = t.day
group by t.kind
order by t.kind

panels.title: Where the nights actually fall
panels.description: The shape behind the scores. A long left tail matters more than the mean moving a point.

targets.rawSql:
select
    readiness_score as "Readiness",
    sleep_score     as "Sleep",
    activity_score  as "Activity"
from daily
where $__timeFilter(day)

panels.title: Calendar load per day
panels.description: Hours of meetings and the hour the day finished. If this is flat and empty, the calendar importer has no feeds configured — which is not the same as a quiet week.

targets.rawSql:
select
    day::timestamptz as "time",
    'Meeting hours' as metric,
    hours as value
from context_daily
where kind = 'meeting' and $__timeFilter(day)
union all
select day::timestamptz, 'Last end hour (local)', last_end_hour
from context_daily
where kind = 'meeting' and $__timeFilter(day)
order by 1
